Definition: from G1 (as a negative particle) and G3539; not to know (through lack of information or intelligence); by implication, to ignore (through disinclination):--(be) ignorant(-ly), not know, not understand, unknown.
BiblicalUsage: Agnoeo is not to know — through lack of information, or through wilful ignorance. The disciples did not understand the saying about the resurrection and were afraid to ask; the Athenians worshipped in ignorance the God Paul proclaimed; Paul warns the Romans not to be ignorant of the mystery of Israel; and he says of the man who is ignorant, let him be ignorant. The word covers honest not-knowing and the kind that refuses to learn — and Scripture treats them very differently.
TheologicalSignificance: What this word teaches me is that ignorance is not one thing. The disciples' fear and the Athenians' altar are met with patience and preaching — but the ignorance that refuses to know is left alone, and I hold that the difference is the willingness to ask.
